title: Colorado Police Warn of 'Jugging' Robberies - NewsBreak
text:
By Matt Sparx ,
2 hours ago
Numerous police departments in Colorado are warning residents of a new type of robbery that has been taking place recently. According to the Lakewood Police Department , criminals are taking money from unsuspecting victims after they have gone to the bank or an ATM.
Canva What Is “Jugging” and How It Works The new tactic for these robberies is called “Jugging,” and there are ways that you can prevent this crime from happening to you.
READ MORE: Colorado Police Warn of New Crime Trend Targeting Residents
Jugging is a form of robbery when a suspect follows the victim immediately after withdrawing money from a financial institution, such as a bank, ATM, or check-cashing store. Suspects usually follow the victim, and when they reach their next destination, this is when the suspect approaches and demands the money. Oftentimes, the perpetrator threatens the victim or uses violence to steal the money, especially if the cash is visible.
What Colorado Police Are Seeing The Lakewood Police Department says that Jugging suspects utilize everyday vehicles to blend in, and the best thing to look out for is behavior as an indicator. Look for vehicles that could be loitering near banks, even taking photos or using binoculars to view what is happening with a cash withdrawal. Also, you should be aware of your surroundings after leaving the bank, as these criminals will follow your vehicle to your next location.
READ MORE: How to Protect Yourself From Scams in Colorado
Here are a few tips that were shared by law enforcement that can keep you safe and not be a victim of a Jugging robbery:
Stay vigilant of your surroundings Do not leave cash in your vehicle Change routes on your commutes to and from work and home Carry cash, cards, and checks discreetly Call 911 if you believe you are being followed More information on this new Jugging robbery trend can be seen on the Lakewood Police Department’s X page .
Infamous Colorado Crimes Take a look at some of Colorado's most notorious crimes. Gallery Credit: Kelsey Nistel Chaffee County Sheriff's Office/Facebook Morphew Murder The murder of Suzanne Morphew has been featured across national news and was even the subject of a recent "48 Hours" episode . The Chaffee County resident went for a bike ride on May 10, 2020, and never returned home. Her body has yet to be found, but Morphew's husband, Barry, has since been arrested for killing his wife. Getty Images Mysterious Death of JonBenét Ramsey The murder of JonBenét Ramsey was a highly publicized Colorado case that remains unsolved to this day. The 6-year-old girl was killed in her Boulder home on Christmas Eve 1996, but the person responsible for her death has never been named. Since the crime took place, there have been many TV documentaries, movies and books published that focus on this tragic murder. RJ Sangosti - Pool/Getty Images Watts Family Murder This unfortunate situation unfolded in Frederick, Colorado, and involved Christopher Watts taking the lives of his pregnant wife, Shanann, and two daughters, during the early morning hours on August 13, 2018. The tragic tale was retold in a Lifetime movie and also made into a true-crime Netflix doc in 2020 . It was also highlighted on the ABC News series 20/20 , and has been reviewed on a variety of other TV programs, including Dr. Phil and The Dr. Oz Show. La Plata County Sheriff's Office/Facebook Redwine Murder The 2012 murder of 13-year-old Dylan Redwine stunned Colorado residents as well as many other people around the country. Authorities searched for the Colorado Springs boy's body for more than four years, after he went missing while visiting his father in Vallecito over Thanksgiving. Dylan's father, Mark Redwine, was ultimately arrested in connection with his son's disappearance and death. Jen Theodore/Unsplash Coors Kidnapping/Murder On February 9, 1960, the grandson of the founder of Coors Brewing Company, Adolph Coors III, was on his way to the office in Golden, Colorado when he was kidnapped by a prison escapee named Joseph Corbett . Months after his disappearance, the remains of Ad Coors were eventually found at a Douglas County dump. Corbett was sentenced to life in prison for the murder but ended up taking his own life in 1980. Because of the notoriety of Coors, the crime made international headlines when it happened. Joshua Hoehne/Unsplash Columbine Shooting April 20, 1999, was a horrifying day in Colorado's history. The mass shooting that took place at Columbine High School sadly took the lives of 12 students and one teacher. Another 21 people were also injured in the attack. The two shooters ended up killing themselves on the scene. The horrific crime made international news, and media outlets continue to talk about it annually. Kevork Djansezian/Getty Images Aurora Theater Shooting People around the world woke up to the news of another terrifying time in Colorado's history on July 20, 2012. This was when James Holmes went on a shooting rampage during a midnight screening of the 'The Dark Knight Rises" in an Aurora movie theater. Holmes was charged with 24 counts of murder and 116 counts of attempted murder. As a result of the shooting, Warner Bros. studios canceled several scheduled premieres. The shooting also spearheaded the "No Notoriety" campaign, in which media outlets are encouraged to limit the use of the photo and name of the suspect in these types of cases.
